**SE-11. Tool roster and `equip_tool`.** *Rule.* The hand rail's tool slots are fixed: **1 `tool_cutter`, 2 `tool_welder`, 3 `tool_scanner`**; slots 4, 5 and 6 are unbound in the MVP (slot 4 was `tool_suppressant`, removed from the MVP kit by the 2026-10-27 ruling on OQ-34, Option A) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Suit registers exactly one command type, **`equip_tool {slot: 1..6}`** — origin PLAYER, `actor_binding OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, `coalesce NONE`, `max_age_ticks` 120 (the Controller's discrete-verb value), payload within `MAX_PAYLOAD`; the Controller's `tool_cycle` input is resolved by the Adapter to a slot (the Adapter, not the simulation, picks "next"). `validate` (immediate class, in this order): kernel authority; **`NOT_ACTIONABLE`** in STAGGERED, DOWNED or DEAD; **`BUSY`** while carrying a module or channelling; **`EMPTY_SLOT`** for slot 4, 5 or 6 or a tool the seat does not hold *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. `apply` sets `equipped_slot`; equipping the already-equipped slot is an accepted no-op. **Sim swap duration 0 ticks:** `apply` sets `equipped_slot` in the tick the command is applied, and `tool_in_hand` answers the new tool from that tick; the Controller's hand animation is presentation only and gates no command (so Sanity's rung-2 scan cost `T_EQUIP`, D.7, is exactly 0 ticks, OQ-SN-6); no noise; **never `allowed_when_paused`** (SE-32). The hand rail also shows the glowstick count and the carried module as passive entries (SE-30). *(Interaction's designed command table lists `equip_tool` as Suit's only command and registers no `use_item` (AC-IA-1); `use_item` is routed to the kernel and Item DB owners as a stale token. A use verb that acts on the world is Interaction's and calls Suit's `consume_charge`; the suppressant's effect is Attention's and Horror's and returns with the item at Vertical Slice.)* *Why.* A tool slot is a Suit fact; what a tool does is the system it acts on. *Rejected.* A holster slot 0 (no MVP verb needs a holstered state; bare-hand verbs declare no tool requirement — Interaction's); equip time (a tell-window exploit in either direction); auto-equip on target (removes a Suit decision and makes `equip_tool` pointless). *Criterion.* AC-SE-13: `equip_tool` on a carrying seat answers `BUSY`; slot 5 answers `EMPTY_SLOT`; while paused it is rejected. *Pillar.* P2 (no equipping with time stopped mid-tell), anti-pillar not a combat game (a slot, not a loadout screen).

**SE-12. Holder model.** *Rule.* Suit owns the three holder classes defined by the Item DB (IDB-16 "the Item DB defines what a thing is; the holder owns who has it and how many"): **HAND** (tool instances — unique per player, one of each `tool_*`, `stack_max` 1), **STOWED** (counted entries in the block, one stack per `def_id`, merged per IDB-15 when `def_id`, `condition_bp` and `charge` are equal), and **CARRIED** (the single carried instance — the Controller owns `carry_ref`, Suit owns the instance and the stored `carried_id`). All modules and the curio are CARRIED; tools are HAND; parts and glowsticks are STOWED. A refused merge leaves the surplus where it was ("the merge is refused by the holder (Suit) and the surplus stays where it was"). The persisted, hashed and replicated form of every instance Suit holds is the Item DB's positional array from `to_array()` = [def_id, count, condition_bp, cap_bp, patched_at_step, charge] (always six elements, every number an int, canonical zeros), decoded only by `from_array(a, graph_step_no)`; Suit never hand-builds an instance Dictionary *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: Item DB IDB-15, registry `item_instance_to_array`; Suit adopts the owner's published canonical form)*; masses and classes are looked up from the static catalogue and never saved. **Suit mints no ids**: the only id it stores is the carried one, passed in by `set_carried`; stowed stacks carry no ids. There is no pack capacity and no weight limit — the carrying cost is the mass cue (SE-28) and, for a carried module, the Controller's `V_CARRY` (no run). *Why.* One owner for "who holds what"; a pack grid or weight cap is an inventory screen by another name (Item DB OQ 6). *Rejected.* A pack grid or total-weight cap. *Criterion.* AC-SE-14: a merge-and-refuse table test over `part_hull_plate` (×1), `part_duct_coupling` (×4) and `cons_glowstick` (×4). *Pillar.* P5, anti-pillar no inventory.

**SE-13. The carried instance and the one mover.** *Rule.* `set_carried(player_id, instance_id, instance)` stores the instance; `release_carried(player_id)` removes it and returns `(instance_id, instance)`, where `instance` is the six-element `to_array()` array of SE-12, stored and returned with every element unchanged (the identity rule, so the Interaction launder fix holds end to end) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. **Suit never self-releases.** On `locomotion_cap` NONE the Controller clears `carry_ref` and **Interaction** converts it to a loose item next tick by calling `release_carried`. Stagger does not drop the module; downed does. `post_restore` checks `controller.state.carry_ref == suit.state.carried_id` (or both NONE) and fails `SUIT_RESTORE_CARRY_MISMATCH` otherwise. The loose-world owner and the instance-id counter are not Suit's: Interaction's designed IA-28 owns `loose[]` and the id counter in `interaction.state`; Suit stores only the id it is handed, and its text holds under any owner. *Why.* Exactly one mover prevents a module existing in two holders at once. *Rejected.* Suit allocating ids (two allocators collide). *Criterion.* AC-SE-15: a carry dropped on DOWNED round-trips to a loose item with identical instance fields; a restore with a mismatched `carry_ref` fails with the named reason. *Pillar.* P1 (the world holds each thing once).

- **L-2I, a second instrument survives.** For one seat, no loop may have every instrument lying at once. The honest second instrument for a loop is one of: a fixed gauge on the same loop in another compartment; `suit.o2` (the occupant compartment's `p_o2`, Suit VA-16) or `suit.warmth` (that compartment's T and P, Suit VA-19; credited for the COOLANT loop's thermal quantity only, QA-3), each valid **only for the seat's current compartment**; or the scanner (`tool_scanner`, honest in the MVP, SN-19), credited **only if the seat carries it and can equip it** (a seat without the scanner has no honest second instrument on a single-instrument loop, so a lie on that loop is ineligible for that seat, QA-2). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review, BLOCKING: two limits. **(1) Direction.** `suit.o2` and `suit.warmth` are credited only for an ALARM-direction lie (L-D). For a COMFORT-direction lie L-G requires the seat's current compartment band to be OK, so those readings agree with the lie while it is legal and the credit would always be empty; a comfort lie needs a fixed gauge on the loop or the scanner. **(2) Carrying.** "Can equip it" means the seat is not carrying a module: Suit SE-11 answers `equip_tool` with `BUSY` while carrying, so a seat that carries cannot reach the scanner. A single-instrument-loop lie is therefore not created for a carrying seat, and a PENDING one is INVALIDATED at its activation re-check if the seat is carrying then; once ACTIVE the lie is not re-evaluated against carrying (the same no-uncaused-vanish reason as doors and dropped scanners). The seat drops the module to scan, which is a priced act, not an exploit.)* `suit.integrity`, `suit.reserve` and `suit.charge` measure the suit, not a ship loop, and never count. For POWER, FUEL, COOLANT flow and INTEGRITY only another fixed gauge on the loop or the scanner counts. In the VS-A slice where readings or the scanner may lie, at least one honest instrument must remain per loop per seat (`SECOND_INSTRUMENT_MIN` 1). **L-2I is evaluated at activation.** After activation it INVALIDATES the lie only when a fixed gauge it relied on is destroyed or lost; it is never re-evaluated on seat movement, on a dropped scanner (the scanner stays in the world) or on a door crossing, because a lie that vanished when the seat walked through a door would be an uncaused-vanish tell (QA-2). *(Orchestrator ruling: the rulings' "a gauge on the same loop elsewhere" is unsatisfiable for the slice's single-instrument loops, one fuel tank sight-glass and one reservoir, pump and radiator set; R23's own words "solo MVP needs rung 2 that does not need a walk" are the warrant for counting the scanner and the two loop-quantity Suit readings; checkpoint K2 removed the three Suit keys that measure the suit.)*

I'm treating this as acceptable at the D.1/D.10 input-stub level, then moving on to consider stage effects at lower level thresholds.

I'm now defining "contact" for multi-horror cases: once horrors enter range together, they stay until all pay values hit zero, then leave together and need 600 consecutive out-of-range runs to reset. I'm settling on one request per (blocker, target) pair rather than strictly one per target file — so the first sanity request bundles AC-SN-25, D.10, and optionally EC-SN-19. Then separate requests follow for AC-SN-151, perception-filter's AC-PF-23, a larger sanity bundle covering SN-16, AC-SN-123, AC-SN-150, EC rules, AC-181, the states table and counts, then the suit reads update, and finally the tool_held addition under suit-and-equipment.

For the counts, I'm working out that adding new auto-checks AC-SN-181 and AC-SN-182 bumps automated checks to 136, making live total 168 (136 auto + 18 lint + 8 review + 6 manual), and with 27 deferred that gives 195 overall — I'll fold this count correction into the final sanity request.

Now I'm drafting the actual change text for request 5: adding a new bullet to SN-16 explaining what happens when a compartment change fires while events are held mid-batch — the held events get discarded, evented[] is cleared, no debounce stamp or draw occurs, batch_end_run resets, and entry_pending gets set for the new compartment so a later visit can form a fresh event without leftover debounce history.

For the debounce clause, I'm rewriting it to clarify both reference points are processing runs (batch close or formation run if the window is closed) rather than raw event runs, since the stamp is written near formation+10, so spacing can drift from exactly 100 by up to the batch length.

Then I'm starting on a new acceptance criterion, AC-SN-123, covering a seat entering a lit compartment at run 1000 where the batch opens immediately.

I'm walking through the timeline: the first event processes at P=1010 and passes the debounce with stamp 1010; a re-entry processed at P+99=1109 gets refused (no draw, counter, or stamp change, subject stays in evented[]); but a re-entry processed at P+100=1110 passes and triggers the remaining gates, with the stamp updating to 1110. I'm also noting a pitfall: the re-entry must happen after the seat leaves, so I need to test both a batch opening at 1099 (closing at 1109) and one at 1100 (closing at 1110) to hit both boundary cases correctly.

Now I'm specifying AC-SN-123: the debounce measured across processing runs passes at exactly 100 and is blocked at 99.

I'm then drafting EC-SN-64 and AC-SN-181, covering a seat entering compartment B at run 2000 with S1/S2 lit and events held until batch_end_run 2010, then the compartment changing at run 2005 — same run, no events fire, no debounce stamps, no draws, counters stay put, batch_end_run clears, and entry_pending gets set, with nothing processed at run 2010. I'm also covering the edge where leaving happens exactly at 2010 (same outcome as the change) versus leaving at 2011 (both events processed with stamp 2010), plus a re-entry at run 2020 forming and processing cleanly at 2030 since no prior stamp exists to trigger debounce refusal, and I'm considering adding a save/restore check at run 2007 to confirm state consistency.

I'm updating the entry_pending states table to note it clears when the compartment changes, which also empties evented[], discards held events, and clears batch_end_run per SN-16, and I'm deciding to describe batch_end_run's cleared state simply as "cleared to its no-batch value" rather than specifying an exact representation.

Now I'm drafting sanity edits for request 6, replacing the Suit Data row to describe Suit's published reads under SE-40 — carried_instance and tool_held — and defining two Sanity-internal derived predicates, carrying and scanner_equippable, built from those reads.

I'm replacing the "Provisional contract" note with a resolved ruling (G1/G6/R9) stating the contract is now Suit's published SE-40, with a stub fallback only for unbound views in tests, and I'm flagging that the suit_read_stub_hits debug counter must be zero in the MVP slice. I'm also noting that Sanity deliberately doesn't use tool_in_hand since it only reflects the equipped tool, not a stowed one, and I'm starting on request 7's SE-40 reads table, adding the tool_held row keyed by suit.state.tools.

I'm finishing the tool_held definition — true whenever the scanner sits in tools regardless of equipped_slot, false once absent, with carried_instance resolved to NONE or a matching instance — then updating AC-SE-68, the Sanity dependency rows (L488, L1127), and the registry entry alongside stowed_heavy. I'm tagging each clause with its kind (INTERNAL, GAP, CONFLICT) based on whether Sanity or Suit owns the acceptance criteria, deciding to skip the advisor call since the work is simulation-verified, and now composing the final output.

input.notes: All four blockers are covered across three files (sanity-and-hallucination-rules, perception-filter, suit-and-equipment); none touches the epoch (R13/R14), and the Sanity GDD already carries the R13/R14 wording, so no epoch requests are needed. Blocker 1 (INTERNAL, G3/G4): I simulated D.1/D.10 at registry defaults and recomputed every oracle as "first run with level < 15000" (k=1 from 70000 is run 18053; from 43000 it is 9053; k=2/3/4 from 43000 are 3917, 2816 and 2050, with the E1 state fixed as a ring-1 home body, settled forced false). The old 9150 and 2175 are end-of-encounter figures, and D.10's own k>=2 contact lengths (163/244/325) were wrong under its marginal-charge rule (true 173/304/343), so D.10 is corrected too, or it would still contradict the AC. Blocker 2: AC-SN-151 now asserts exactly one NEEDLE or READOUT entry and no card entry. The never-the-truth half moves to AC-PF-23 in the Perception Filter. Blocker 3: the debounce oracle is restated on processing runs (P+99 refused, P+100 passes), the discard-held-events-on-compartment-change rule is added to SN-16 with EC-SN-64 and AC-SN-181, and AC-SN-150 is aligned. Blocker 4 (CONFLICT plus a GAP, G1/G6): Sanity drops carry_state and scanner_equippable as Suit names and reads Suit's published carried_instance (compared with NONE, not 0, since that is Suit's return) plus a new Suit-added pure read tool_held(player_id, def_id), because tool_in_hand names only the equipped tool and Suit has no other way to say the scanner is held. I judged that a minimal owner addition, not a removal of the ruled comfort-lie behaviour. The stub stays only for a missing view, and a debug counter plus AC-SN-182 prove the MVP slice never takes the stub path. Counts become 168 live / 27 deferred / 195 total. Orchestrator follow-up: register tool_held in design/registry/entities.yaml next to stowed_heavy, since the registry is not a plannable target here.
